# Bank Loans

A player (human or AI) who cannot pay their end-of-turn costs can take a bank loan
instead of going bankrupt: a fixed principal is credited immediately and repaid as a
fixed per-turn amount (principal + 10% total interest) until the term expires. Loans
cost no action point and there is at most one active loan per player.

## Problem statement

Bankruptcy is currently a terminal state (`checkImmediateLoss` fires at `coins < 0`,
`resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` eliminates an AI seat), so a single bad week ends a
run with no recovery path. Players also have no way to convert future income into
present cash, which narrows strategic options in the mid-game. Bank Loans add a
credit mechanic that lets a player buy their way past a cash crunch at the cost of a
fixed debt burden.

## Users

- **Human player (single- and competitive mode)** — "When my end-of-turn costs leave
  me at negative coins, I want to be offered a loan so I can keep playing instead of
  losing the run."
- **Human player, mid-game** — "When I am short of the cash for a strong move at the
  end of a turn, I want to borrow a fixed amount with a repayment schedule I can see,
  so I can judge whether the debt is worth it."
- **AI opponent (competitive mode)** — "When I go bankrupt I should be given the same
  bailout a human gets, so an unlucky week does not knock me out of the game."

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Loan offer & taking a loan.** A seat with no active loan can take a loan by choosing one option from the configured loan menu (default: 300 coins / 3 turns, 600 / 6, 1000 / 10). Taking a loan credits the principal to that seat's wallet immediately, records the active loan, and **costs no action point** (`actionsRemaining` unchanged).
2. **One active loan per player.** A seat that already has an active loan cannot take or accept another one; the attempt is rejected with a clear, user-facing reason and no resource change.
3. **Fixed per-turn repayment.** At the end of every turn in which a seat holds an active loan, exactly `perTurnRepayment` coins are deducted from that seat's wallet (`totalRepayment = round(principal × 1.10)`, `perTurnRepayment = round(totalRepayment / termTurns)`; e.g. 600 / 6 → 110 per turn, 660 total). The deduction is recorded in the turn's net summary as a one-off expense; the loan is retired after `termTurns` payments and no further deductions occur.
4. **Bankruptcy bailout.** When a seat would fail on `coins < 0` (single-player loss, or competitive seat failure) **and holds no active loan**, the game does not end (and the seat is not eliminated): a loan offer is presented instead. Accepting credits the principal and play continues; declining, or already holding an active loan, preserves today's bankruptcy behaviour. At most one bailout offer is made per seat per turn (no offer loop).
5. **AI bailout policy.** An AI seat that hits `coins < 0` with no active loan auto-accepts the **largest** loan option and is not eliminated; an AI seat that already holds an active loan is eliminated exactly as today. AI seats take no proactive (non-bailout) loans.
6. **Visible obligation.** While a loan is active the player can see what they owe: the activity log records the loan (amount, per-turn repayment, term) and the remaining obligation (turns left + per-turn amount) is surfaced in the HUD, so the debt burden is never hidden.
7. **Repayment shortfall.** Repayment is deducted unconditionally, so a payment that exceeds the seat's balance leaves `coins < 0` and triggers the normal bankruptcy path — which offers a bailout only if the seat has no active loan (per AC4), i.e. a seat already repaying a loan simply goes bankrupt.
8. **Headless determinism.** Headless turn execution (`endTurnHeadless`, Monte Carlo, balance runs) never stalls on a pending loan offer: it resolves deterministically using the AC5 AI policy, and simulations without loans enabled are byte-identical to today's results.
9. **Persistence and back-compatibility.** Active loans and a pending offer survive a save/load round-trip; pre-loan saves (schema v2) load with no loans and unchanged behaviour. Save schema version is bumped with a migration.
10. **Testing/validation.** New unit tests cover the loan maths (option table, `perTurnRepayment`, retirement after `termTurns`), single-loan enforcement, bailout offer/accept/decline, shortfall → bankruptcy, AI largest-option policy, headless resolution and save/load round-trip; the competitive-seat path is covered by an integration test.
11. **Documentation.** All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md`, and the in-game help content where it lists end-of-turn economy rules.
12. **Full project test suite must pass** with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **No action point cost** — taking a loan must not decrement `actionsRemaining`
  (seed requirement).
- **Fixed menu, no negotiation** — the loan menu is configuration data
  (`config.loanOptions`), identical for every seat in a run; no per-seat or
  per-difficulty negotiation UI. Re-balancing is a config edit only.
- **Interest model** — flat 10% of principal over the whole term, spread evenly
  (`600 / 6 → 110/week`, per the seed's worked example). No compounding, no
  per-turn-on-outstanding-balance interest.
- **One active loan per player** (producer decision Q1 = A) — no debt stacking.
- **Bailout-only AI** (Q3 = A) — AI strategy changes are limited to auto-accepting a
  bailout offer; no new AI heuristics otherwise.
- **Economy realism** — repayment moves through the existing `EconomyLedger` /
  `resourceBank` sync path; no direct wallet mutation.
- **Config defaults** — `loansEnabled: true` in the `Easy`/`Medium`/`Hard` presets
  (the mechanic is live in the game), and `false` for headless/simulation configs so
  existing Monte Carlo and balance baselines stay unchanged until a simulation opts in.
- **No turn-summary dependency** — the Turn Summary dialog
  (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) does not exist yet; this item must not block on it.

## Existing state

- Bankruptcy is terminal and evaluated in two places:
  `checkImmediateLoss` (single-player, `coins < 0` → `endReason 'bankruptcy'`) and
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures` (competitor seats; human → loss, AI →
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`), both in `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts`.
  An opening-day grace already exists (`applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`,
  MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41), which bailout evaluation must respect.
- Pending-decision pausing is an established pattern: `state.pendingEventChoice` and
  `state.pendingPiggyback` both defer the closing tail and are resolved by the UI
  before the closing re-runs — a pending loan offer should follow the same shape.
- Turn economy closes in `processEndOfTurn` (income, ongoing costs, incident) and
  summarises into the activity log via `appendTurnNetRow`; a repayment expense belongs
  in that same sequence so the net row reflects it.
- Per-seat wallets live in `state.players[].coins` (competitive) while
  `state.resourceBank` is the working mirror bound by `bindCompetitiveSeat` /
  `restoreCompetitiveSeat`; `state.players` is `undefined` in single-player.
- `GameConfig` (`src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts`) is a numeric-parameter bag derived from
  difficulty presets, consumed by the engine — the natural home for loan config.
- No loan code exists anywhere in the repo (`grep -ri loan src core tests docs` is
  empty) — this is net-new capability.
- Save/load uses `serializeMainStreetState` / `deserializeMainStreetState` with a
  strict schema-version check (`MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION = 2`) and a migration
  hook, so a version bump plus defaults is the established path for new fields.

## Desired change

1. **Loan model** — new `LoanOption` / `ActiveLoan` types and `MainStreetLoans.ts`
   holding the option table, offer computation, and pure apply/resolve helpers.
   State gains `loans: ActiveLoan[]` (invariant: at most one entry per `ownerId`) and
   `pendingLoanOffer?: { ownerId, reason, options }`.
2. **Config** — `loansEnabled`, `loanInterestRate` (0.10) and `loanOptions` added to
   `GameConfig` and all difficulty presets (`loansEnabled: true`); headless/simulation
   configs default it to `false` so existing balance baselines are unchanged.
3. **Taking a loan** — a `takeLoan` command (no AP cost) validated against the
   one-active-loan rule, crediting principal via the ledger and logging the decision.
4. **Repayment** — `applyLoanRepayments(state)` invoked in the closing sequence ahead
   of the end-condition checks, decrementing `turnsRemaining` and logging the expense
   into the turn net row.
5. **Bailout offer** — `maybeOfferBailout(state)` evaluated *before* the bankruptcy /
   seat-failure declarations: when a seat with no active loan is at `coins < 0`, set
   `pendingLoanOffer` (reason `bankruptcy`) and pause the closing instead of ending the
   game; `acceptLoanOffer` / `declineLoanOffer` resume it. Declining, a second offer in
   the same turn, or an already-active loan preserves current behaviour.
6. **Visible obligation** — log the loan at acceptance and surface
   "Loan: X coins/turn, N turns left" in the HUD beside the coin/reputation readouts.
7. **UI** — a bailout overlay (option list with per-turn and total repayment shown,
   plus Decline) rendered when a pending offer exists, wiring the deferred-closing
   resume path in `MainStreetTurnController`. The mid-game entry point on the Turn
   Summary dialog is **out of scope** here (see Non-goals).
8. **AI** — bailout auto-accept of the largest option in the AI/headless path.
9. **Persistence** — serialise `loans` and `pendingLoanOffer`; bump the save schema to
   v3 with a migration defaulting legacy saves to an empty loan list.

### Non-goals / out of scope

- Wiring the "Bank Loan" button into the Turn Summary dialog
  (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) — a thin follow-up once that dialog lands. Per producer
  decision Q4, **if the dialog is not completed in time, raise a separate follow-up
  work item** for the wiring rather than expanding this item.
- Multiple concurrent/stacked loans, variable or negotiated interest, per-seat credit
  limits.
- Deducting outstanding principal from the score, or any loan effect on reputation.
- Proactive (non-bailout) AI loan strategy.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/MainStreetLoans.ts` — **new**. Option table (`DEFAULT_LOAN_OPTIONS`), repayment
  maths, `takeLoan`, `applyLoanRepayments`, `maybeOfferBailout`,
  `acceptLoanOffer` / `declineLoanOffer`, active-loan lookup per owner.
- `src/MainStreetStateTypes.ts` — `LoanOption`, `ActiveLoan`, `PendingLoanOffer`
  types; `loans` and `pendingLoanOffer` fields on `MainStreetState`.
- `src/MainStreetDifficulty.ts` — `loansEnabled`, `loanInterestRate`, `loanOptions` on
  `GameConfig` plus all presets (`Easy`/`Medium`/`Hard`).
- `src/MainStreetEngineTurnClosing.ts` — call `applyLoanRepayments` and
  `maybeOfferBailout` ahead of `checkImmediateLoss` / `checkEndConditions` /
  `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`; defer the closing tail while an offer is pending.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererHud.ts` — active-loan readout (turns left,
  per-turn repayment) beside the coin/reputation HUD.
- `src/MainStreetHelpContent.ts` — end-of-turn economy help text: loan menu and
  bailout rule.
- `src/MainStreetEngineTypes.ts` — `pendingLoanOffer` on `TurnResult` (mirroring
  `choicePending` / `piggybackPending`) and a `TakeLoanAction` in `PlayerAction`.
- `src/MainStreetEngineCommands.ts`, `src/MainStreetCommands.ts` — `takeLoan` handler
  and command dispatch; assert no AP consumption.
- `src/MainStreetAiStrategy.ts` — bailout auto-accept (largest option) for AI seats.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLoanOverlay.ts` — **new**. Bailout dialog: option rows with
  per-turn/total repayment, Accept and Decline.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnController.ts`, `src/scenes/MainStreetOverlayContent.ts`,
  `src/scenes/MainStreetGameOverSummary.ts` — show the overlay instead of the game-over
  summary while a bailout offer is open; resume the deferred closing on resolution.
- `src/MainStreetStateSerialize.ts`, `src/MainStreetSaveLoad.ts` — serialise/restore
  loans and the pending offer; bump `MAIN_STREET_SAVE_SCHEMA_VERSION` to 3 with a
  migration.
- `src/MainStreetMonteCarlo.ts` — headless deterministic resolution of a pending offer.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoans.test.ts` — **new**. Maths, one-loan rule, config.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanBailout.test.ts` — **new**. Bailout offer/accept/
  decline, shortfall, AI policy, headless.
- `tests/main-street/MainStreetLoanSaveLoad.test.ts` — **new**. Round-trip + v2
  migration.
- `docs/game/core-rules-and-mechanics.md` — economy section: loan menu, repayment
  schedule, bailout rule.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption — interest arithmetic.** The seed's worked example (600 over 6 turns at
  110/turn = 660 total) is read as "10% of principal over the whole term, spread
  evenly", not "10% per turn on the outstanding balance" (which would be ~137/turn).
  Low risk: the example is unambiguous arithmetic; a config-driven `loanInterestRate`
  makes the alternative a one-line change.
- **Assumption — default option menu.** Three options (300/3, 600/6, 1000/10) all
  yielding 110/turn are proposed so the producer's choice (Q2 = B, "a choice among
  options") has a concrete, balanced default. Pure config data; re-balancing needs no
  code change.
- **Assumption — loans do not affect scoring.** Debt only drains coins; outstanding
  principal is not deducted from `finalScore`. Recorded as a possible follow-up rather
  than scope.
- **Risk — end-condition ordering.** The bailout intercept must run *before*
  `checkImmediateLoss` / `resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, and must respect the
  existing first-turn solvency grace, or the game will end before the offer is shown.
  Mitigation: explicit ordering tests plus a per-turn "already offered" guard.
- **Risk — deferred closing loops.** Reusing the `pendingLoanOffer` pause means the
  closing can be re-entered; an unresolvable offer (decline with no other option) must
  converge to game over in one pass. Mitigation: idempotency tests and the per-turn
  offer guard.
- **Risk — headless/Monte Carlo regressions.** A pending offer that blocks headless
  closing would hang balance runs. Mitigation: AC7 determinism tests plus
  `loansEnabled: false` default for simulation configs, with before/after result
  comparison.
- **Risk — save schema.** Bumping the shared save schema risks older-campaign
  compatibility. Mitigation: v2 migration test that loads a pre-loan save unchanged.
- **Risk — scope creep.** The Turn Summary dialog entry point, proactive AI lending and
  score effects are natural "while we're here" additions; each is recorded as a
  non-goal/follow-up rather than absorbed into this item.

## Related work

- **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41 — End of Turn summary** (stage `idea`). Defines the
  turn-summary dialog with a "Bank Loan" button that is explicitly waiting on this
  feature. **Related, not blocking**: this item ships the engine, bailout flow and
  `takeLoan` command without it; the dialog wiring is a follow-up (see Non-goals).
- **MS-0MUWE6MSQ006DEZ4 — End-reason & player-state model** (completed). Introduced the
  `EndReason` union (`bankruptcy`, `reputation_collapse`, …) and the per-seat failure
  badges that the bailout path intercepts.
- **MS-0MUVQRBVI0015AB2 — AI seat elimination / last standing** (completed via
  `eliminateCompetitiveSeat`, `checkLastStanding`). The bailout must run before
  elimination so an AI survives, which in turn delays last-standing wins.
- **MS-0MVJNFESC005QJ41 — Play Again does not reset the AI** (completed). Also
  introduced the opening-day solvency grace (`applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`) that
  bailout evaluation must respect.
- **MS-0MUWDL0V40041USM — Provide reason for game ending** (completed). Game-over
  copy/end-reason surfacing that the "declined bailout" path must still produce.
- **MS-0MUYC47EL005Z69H / CG-0MTSHG8RP008E128 — pending-decision pausing**
  (`pendingEventChoice`, `pendingPiggyback`). The `pendingLoanOffer` pause should
  follow this established deferred-closing pattern.
- Duplicate check performed — no completed item covers bank loans; the only overlap is
  the turn-summary dialog item above (partial relationship, not a duplicate).

## Appendix: clarifying questions & answers

Round 1

- **Q1: Can a player hold more than one loan at once?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — one active loan per player; further
  offers deferred until it is repaid.** Source: interactive reply, session
  `herdr-1792944777-2932233-30937`.
- **Q2: What shape is the loan offer?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **B — a choice among options (e.g. 300/3,
  600/6), pick one.** Source: interactive reply, same session. Consequence: the brief
  defines a config-driven option menu rather than a single fixed offer.
- **Q3: How do AI opponents use loans?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — bankruptcy bailout only; auto-accept
  when an AI seat hits `coins < 0`.** Source: interactive reply, same session.
  Consequence: no proactive AI lending in this item.

Round 2

- **Q4: Entry point while the Turn Summary dialog does not exist yet?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — build the loan engine + `takeLoan`
  command + bankruptcy-bailout UI now; wire the Turn-summary "Bank Loan" button when
  that dialog lands, and create a follow-up item if the dialog has not been completed
  in time.** Source: interactive reply, same session.
- **Q5: Which option does an AI auto-accept on bailout?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — the largest available option.** Source:
  interactive reply, same session.
- **Q6: Repayment shortfall behaviour?**
  — Answer (producer, interactive reply): **A — deduct anyway; negative coins trigger
  the existing bankruptcy flow, and a seat that already holds a loan gets no new
  offer.** Source: interactive reply, same session.

Research notes: repo searched for existing loan code (`grep -ri loan src core tests
docs` — no matches) and for the bankruptcy hooks (`checkImmediateLoss`,
`resolveCompetitiveSeatFailures`, `applyFirstSharedDaySolvencyGrace`). Related
work items found via `wl search "loan"` / `wl search "bankrupt"`; the turn-summary
dependency item (MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41) was read in full and is at stage `idea`.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items

When all animations for the End of Turn phase have completed we should pop up a dialog with details of the current state of the game. # of businesses owned by each player, income and expenses for that turn, one-off income/expenses (from events etc.) and any other information that would be useful and informative. The dialog will have a "next turn" button and a "Bank Loan" button which will allow them to take out a loan (a feature not yet implemented, see work item) (open)
- **MS-0MUTU8IYV0086PF6** – Competitive turn orchestration in the scene (completed)
- **MS-0MUTU8J9T0034OT7** – Competitive scoreboard & active-seat HUD (completed)

# `implement.py phase_start` records the worktree as `repo_root` on resume-from-worktree

discovered-from:MS-0MVLINWHE004W4CP

## Problem statement

`phase_start` resolves the main checkout root correctly at Step 6.5
(`repo_root = _get_repo_root() or ...`) but then **recomputes it from
`Path.cwd()` at Step 8** and writes that value into
`.implement_state.json`. When `start` is run as a resume from inside an
existing worktree — the normal driven-child pattern — `cwd` *is* the
worktree, so the state file records the worktree as `repo_root` and every
downstream consumer of that value is wrong: `phase_finish` cannot fast-forward
`dev` in the main checkout, and its worktree-removal gate refuses to remove
"the repository root", so a successfully pushed implementation is left
stranded with the work item reset to `open`.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer** resuming a driven child session or re-running `start`
  in an existing worktree: needs `start` → `finish` to work unchanged, with no
  manual state-file surgery.
- **Parent/phase session** orchestrating children: a stranded child leaves the
  parent phase unable to close the epic and burns a session on recovery.
- **Maintainer** reading `.implement_state.json`: needs `repo_root` to mean one
  thing — the main checkout — so state is diagnosable.

Example user stories:

> As a driven child session resuming its worktree, I want `implement.py start`
> to record the main checkout root, so that `finish` can fast-forward `dev`
> and remove my worktree.

> As a parent session, I want a child that already has a bad state file to
> still finish cleanly, so that I do not have to hand-edit JSON to unblock an
> epic.

## Existing state

`skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` (source repo `SorraAgents`; the global
install `~/.pi/agent/skills` is a symlink to `SorraAgents/skill`):

| Line (at `91de33cf5`) | Code | Role |
|---|---|---|
| 4110 | `repo_root = _get_repo_root() or str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | Step 6.5 — correct main-root resolution (used for the parent-branch refresh) |
| 4178 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | **Defect** — Step 8 overwrites the correct value before `_store_signal_globals` / `write_state` |
| 4613-4616 | `repo_root = state.repo_root if state else (...)` | `phase_finish` trusts the (wrong) state value for the `dev` fast-forward, the push and `_sync_parent_branch` |
| 4732 | `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=state.repo_root if state else None)` | Gate 1 compares `worktree_path.resolve()` with `repo_root.resolve()` → `RuntimeError: REFUSE to remove the repository root` |
| 4872 | `repo_root = str(Path.cwd().resolve())` | `phase_abort` Step 3 — same defect class: `_restore_repo_state` runs `git checkout dev` / `git pull` in the worktree, both silently failing (`check=False`) |

Failure sequence observed (resume-from-worktree start):

1. `start` writes `repo_root = <worktree>`; `_store_signal_globals` gets the
   same value, so the SIGTERM handler's `_restore_repo_state` would also run in
   the worktree.
2. `finish` Step 5 tries `git checkout dev` inside the worktree → fails ("already
   checked out"); caught and logged as a warning, so the main checkout is never
   fast-forwarded (the pre-push context-budget gate then works from a stale
   checkout).
3. `finish` Step 6 pushes successfully from the worktree, **then** Step 7 calls
   `_remove_worktree(worktree_path, repo_root=<worktree>)`, which raises the
   safety-gate `RuntimeError`; the outer handler resets the item to `open`,
   posts no completion comment, and leaves the worktree in place.
4. The worktree can then be removed by a later cleanup pass (signal handler /
   parent phase) **while the child session's `cwd` is still inside it** — the
   reported end state: a session stranded on a deleted working directory.
   `_remove_worktree` deliberately `chdir`s to `repo_root` before removal, but
   with the wrong `repo_root` stored it either raises before that `chdir` or
   chdirs into the worktree it is about to delete.

Live evidence of the same defect (recorded during this intake, not fixed here):

```
.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite/.implement_state.json
  "repo_root": ".../.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK-drive-timeout-reconciliation-test-suite"
  "started_at": "2026-10-24T11:11:45Z"
```

(SA-0MVLJWL60001H6QK — Drive timeout-reconciliation test suite — is still
`open`/`intake_complete`; that worktree is the recovery target, not scope of
this item.)

## Desired change

1. **Fix the source of truth.** Make Step 8 use the already-resolved main
   checkout root (reuse the Step 6.5 value / call `_get_repo_root()`), so
   `_store_signal_globals` and the state file always carry the main checkout,
   never the worktree.
2. **Repair stale state defensively.** In `phase_finish` and `phase_abort`,
   treat a `state.repo_root` that resolves to the worktree itself (or to a path
   inside it) as stale and fall back to `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)`; keep
   the correct value for the remaining steps (and, optionally, rewrite the
   state file). This is what unblocks worktrees already stranded by the bug
   **without** hand-editing JSON.
3. **Fix the abort path.** `phase_abort` Step 3 must restore the *main*
   checkout when invoked from inside the worktree.
4. **Regress-proof it.** A test that fails on the pre-fix code: a real
   temporary git repo plus a linked worktree, `cwd` set inside the worktree,
   `start` resumed, asserting the persisted `repo_root` is the main root; plus a
   finish-gate assertion that the worktree path is never handed to
   `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`.

## Implementation plan (test-first)

Ordered so the regression test lands **first** and is proven to fail before
the fix (test-first ordering per the implement skill):

1. **Test (red).** New `skill/implement/tests/test_repo_root_resolution.py`
   using a real `tmp_path` git repo (`git init`, one commit on `dev`) plus a
   linked worktree (`git worktree add`), with no `_get_repo_root` mocking:
   - `cwd` inside the worktree, `phase_start` resumed → `.implement_state.json`
     `repo_root` is the main checkout root and the value handed to
     `_store_signal_globals` matches it;
   - a state file whose `repo_root` is the worktree itself → `phase_finish`'s
     worktree-removal gate succeeds and the worktree path is never passed to
     `_remove_worktree` as `repo_root`;
   - `phase_abort` run from inside the worktree leaves the **main** checkout on
     the parent branch (and behaves identically when run from the main
     checkout).
   Confirm all three fail against the pre-fix code, then keep them passing.
2. **Fix Step 8.** Reuse the already-resolved Step 6.5 `repo_root`
   (`_get_repo_root()`), removing the `Path.cwd()` recomputation, so
   `_store_signal_globals` and `write_state` always carry the main checkout.
3. **Harden `phase_finish`.** Treat a `state.repo_root` equal to, or inside,
   `worktree_path` as stale: log the rejected and derived values at WARNING
   and derive the main root with `_get_repo_root(worktree_path)` (falling back
   to discovery), then use it for the `dev` fast-forward, the push,
   `_sync_parent_branch` and the `_remove_worktree` call.
   `_remove_worktree`'s own gates stay untouched.
4. **Fix `phase_abort` Step 3.** Apply the same stale-state rejection, then
   `_restore_repo_state(main_root)` so `git checkout`/`pull` run in the main
   checkout instead of silently failing inside the worktree.
5. **Docs.** State-file schema note — `repo_root` is always the **main
   checkout** — in `skill/implement/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/worktree-isolation.md`, plus code comments at each corrected
   site.
6. **Verify.** Changed-scope test run then full suite via `/skill:test`;
   commit → push on the SorraAgents `dev` branch (this repo only).

# Enter-to-end-turn browser wait exceeds the 60 s hook above ~2x CPU oversubscription

## Headline

The `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` wait in
`tests/main-street/MainStreetScene.browser.test.ts` is already at the largest
budget the 60 s browser hook permits (40 000 ms = 16 000 ms cap + 24 000 ms
margin + 20 000 ms boot = 60 000 ms), yet it fails at ≈2× CPU oversubscription
because the bounded end-of-turn deferral is re-polled on Phaser's clamped game
clock, so the forced day start is detected late. **Decision: make the
deferral's safety cap starvation-proof** — one extracted helper whose deadline
and re-poll run on wall clock, enforced even while the page is not painting
(producer, Q1 = C, Q2 = 1).

## Problem statement

The soak evidence on MS-0MVLINY2Q004V33L shows the gate passes 20/20 quiet
(peak load 15.3), passes 2/2 at 8 burners (peak 23.6), and fails exactly one
wait — `turn to advance after end-of-turn presentation` — at load ≥ ≈31
(≈2× oversubscription, 16 burners, peak 32.8). That wait's budget is already at
the ceiling the 60 s hook permits, so no poll-budget tweak inside the hook can
rescue it.

Root cause (mechanism, verified against the installed `phaser` source):
Phaser's `TimeStep` clamps the per-frame delta it feeds scenes — under
`smoothStep` (default on) each frame contributes at most `1000/fps.min`
(200 ms) — and `Clock.elapsed`, which drives `delayedCall` timers and tween
progress, advances by that clamped delta. Under starvation (a few frames per
second) all game-time-paced choreography stretches: income phase gaps, coin
flights, the incident hold, and the deferral's own 250 ms `delayedCall`
re-polls. The deferral *deadline* (`s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`,
where `s.time.now` is the raw frame timestamp) is wall-clock, but it is only
re-checked at those clamped polls, so the forced day start is delayed by the
same starvation. Aggregate: closing choreography (stretched) + 16 s cap
(late-detected) + boot > the 40 s budget and the 60 s hook.

The cap's stated purpose is "end-of-turn can never hang the game"
(CG-0MTR72P14000VO6Q, AC5/AC7). A stall bound that is only observed at frame
boundaries does not provide that guarantee — which is what this item fixes,
without touching the user-visible pacing.

## Users

- **Agent-implementer / gate runner** on the shared dev host: needs the browser
  gate green; a red `MainStreetScene` suite at ≈2× oversubscription burns whole
  sessions on retries and blocks the build → test → commit order.
- **Maintainer triaging a red browser suite**: needs a red wait to mean a
  behavioural regression, not host weather.
- **Release engineer** on the dev-push gate: a red gate on a loaded shared host
  stalls shipping even when the scene is correct.
- **Players**: unchanged pacing — the choreography, the incident hold and the
  cap value all stay as shipped; only the cap's *enforcement* becomes
  wall-clock rather than frame-clock, so under starvation the day advances at
  the documented bound instead of stalling past it.

Example user stories:

> As an agent running the browser gate on the shared 16-core host, I want the
> Enter-to-end-turn wait to pass at any load the host actually reaches, so that
> my gate result does not depend on which sibling suites happen to be running.

> As a player whose machine is momentarily overloaded, I want the end-of-turn
> to still advance within the documented safety window, so that the game can
> never appear hung.

## Existing state

- Measured envelope (2026-10-24, 16-core shared host): quiet 20/20 pass
  (peak 15.3); 8 burners 2/2 pass, then one fail at ambient 31.3; 16 burners
  fail at the 40 000 ms end-of-turn budget. Every other wait in the file passes
  at that load.
- The wait's effective budget is `capMs: INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` (16 000) +
  `floorMs: END_TURN_STARVATION_MARGIN_MS` (24 000) = 40 000 ms, the largest
  that keeps the documented 20 000 ms scene-boot allowance inside the 60 s
  `testTimeout` (asserted by `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`). The
  suite's per-test timeout is already `it(..., 60_000)`.
- Five deferral polls race the choreography, all with the same shape
  (`startAt = <scene clock> + cap`, then `delayedCall(250, poll)`):
  3 in `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` (`advanceTurn` ~433,
  forced event-choice ~617, piggyback ~783) and 2 in
  `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` (`finish`'s income wait
  ~254 and the reveal gating ~301).
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerAnimation.ts` already has the
  degradation precedent: `scheduleOrRun` runs the callback immediately when the
  scene has no clock (headless), which a wall-clock helper must preserve.
- Node unit suites drive these polls through fake `time` stubs
  (`tests/main-street/competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
  `tests/main-street/turnflow.test.ts`), and
  `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` pins "exactly three
  `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" by regex — both must be
  updated by the extraction.
- Reduced motion clears `incomeCollectionActive` synchronously in
  `MainStreetAnimatorIncome` (~line 1039), but it is **not** the remedy chosen:
  the parent rejected it as the sole remedy because it removes the
  deferred-income path from coverage.

## Desired change (decision: option C)

Replace the five duplicated deferral polls with **one shared, injectable
helper** that:

1. computes its deadline from a wall-clock timestamp (`Date.now()`),
2. re-polls with a wall-clock timer (`window.setTimeout`), not the scene clock,
3. forces completion (clearing `incomeCollectionActive` and invoking the
   caller's continuation) once `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` of wall time has
   elapsed since the deferral began,
4. is enforced even when the page is not painting — a backgrounded/hidden
   document ahead of the cap forces the advance rather than waiting for the
   next animation frame (Q2 = 1), and
5. degrades to today's behaviour where no clock/timer exists (headless node
   scenes run the continuation immediately), and exposes its clock/timer for
   deterministic unit driving.

Options considered and rejected (recorded for traceability):

- **A — accept and document the envelope** (no code change): the gate can still
  go red on the shared host when ambient load spikes ≥2×, conflicting with the
  "red tree never pushed" policy; rejected in favour of a root-cause fix.
- **B — reduced-motion Enter test + a separate cheap deferral-contract test**:
  no production change, but downgrades the file's end-to-end end-of-turn test
  to a synthetic and couples coverage to a reduced-motion implementation
  detail; retained only as a fallback if C's soak does not pass.
- **D — raise the browser hook for this test**: pure masking, requires
  amending the parent's "any derived budget must leave headroom for boot plus
  teardown within that hook" AC and re-baselining the guard's headroom rule,
  and would fail again at ≈4× oversubscription; rejected.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] **One bounded-deferral helper, wall-clock enforced.** All five
      income-collection deferral polls route through a single shared helper
      whose deadline is wall clock and whose re-poll is a wall timer; no inline
      `s.time.delayedCall(250, <poll>)` / `<scene clock> + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS`
      poll remains. A unit test with a frozen scene clock and an advancing wall
      clock proves the continuation is forced within one poll interval of the
      16 000 ms cap.
- [ ] **Forced advance is not tied to paint.** When the document is hidden / no
      frame runs, the cap still forces the advance after the cap elapses
      (Q2 = 1). A unit test asserts the wall timer — not the scene clock —
      drives the assertion, and the behaviour is documented in the module's
      code comment.
- [ ] **Injectable and backward-compatible.** The helper accepts an injectable
      clock/timer (so `competitive-closing-presentation.test.ts`,
      `turnflow.test.ts` and the new tests drive it deterministically) and
      preserves today's no-clock degradation (headless scenes run the
      continuation immediately).
- [ ] **Single source of truth for the cap.** `INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` stays
      16 000 and remains the only cap value; the
      `tests/main-street/income-collection-cap.test.ts` "exactly three
      `s.time.now + INCOME_COLLECTION_CAP_MS` sites" pin is updated to the
      helper extraction (asserting the helper consumes the constant), so the
      duplication cannot silently return.
- [ ] **No production pacing change.** The choreography timing constants
      (`INCOME_PHASE_GAP_MS`, flight/stagger durations, `INCIDENT_REVEAL_HOLD_MS`)
      and the cap value are unchanged — pinned by existing/added unit tests;
      only the cap's enforcement mechanism differs.
- [ ] **Wait-budget guard still green.** `tests/tooling/wait-budget-guard.test.ts`
      passes unchanged: the end-of-turn wait keeps its cap-derived 40 000 ms
      budget and `budget + 20 s boot ≤ 60 s` headroom rule. If the soak shows
      the budget can now be reduced, that reduction is a *derived* margin
      change proved by the soak, not a hand-picked literal.
- [ ] **Reliability proven, not assumed.** `/skill:test --type soak-load`
      (≥ `nproc` burners) passes with the change, and the pre-change failure at
      the same burner count is reproduced and recorded on this item; both
      before/after tables (burners, peak load, runs, wall times, summary paths)
      are posted as a comment.
- [ ] **Documentation updated.** `docs/dev/testing.md` "Measured envelope" and
      the headroom rule section record the decision (cap enforced on wall
      clock, hidden-tab semantics) and the post-fix envelope, replacing the
      "above ~2× is outside the envelope" caveat with measured evidence; the
      helper's module comment documents the wall-clock contract. All related
      documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments,
      README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

# Intake Brief — Reputation is no longer represented by people walking the streets (MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q)

**Type:** bug (regression) · **Priority:** high · **Stage:** intake

## Headline

The ambient reputation crowd is missing again: the pedestrian silhouette layer shipped in v0.1.19 no longer appears on the street in normal play, so reputation has lost its diegetic on-street presence and the reputation income no longer visibly comes from the people in the shops.

## Problem statement

Reputation used to be represented by a live crowd of small silhouettes that walked the roads and entered occupied businesses; those figures scaled with reputation and sourced the end-of-turn reputation income. The producer reports a regression: the crowd is gone. The layer source and its scene/renderer/turn-flow hooks are still present in `dev`, so the regression is most likely in scene integration or rendering (attach/rebuild ordering, camera/mask, HUD refresh path, reducers that gate rendering, or a layout change that moves the layer off-screen) rather than the feature having been deleted.

## Users

- **Main Street player** — wants to see their reputation as a living street: more reputation means a busier street, and the end-of-turn reputation income visibly comes from the people in their shops.
  - *As a player, I want the street to show how reputable I have become, so progress is legible without reading the HUD.*
  - *As a player, I want the people in my shops to be the source of my reputation income, so the economy feels diegetic.*
- **Producer / game designer** — wants the shipped behaviour restored exactly as documented, not redesigned, and wants a guard so this regression cannot silently return.
- **Developer / QA** — needs the layer to stay presentation-only, deterministic, reduced-motion/replay exempt, and non-blocking, and needs a scene-level test that would have caught the disappearance.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Regression reproduced and root cause recorded.** The work item records a concrete reproduction (mode, difficulty, steps, build/commit) and the change or condition that made the crowd disappear — the offending commit/file where one exists, or the ruled-out alternatives and the failing condition where it does not. The fix commit references that finding. Verified by reading the work-item comment and the fix commit message.
2. **Crowd is visible in normal play.** On a fresh normal-play game (default settings, not Reduced Motion, not replay/headless), once the HUD has rendered the player's starting reputation the street displays `pedestrianCount(state.resourceBank.reputation)` silhouette figures in `PEDESTRIAN_COLOR`, parented to the live street container. Verified by a scene-level browser/behaviour test that boots the real scene and asserts the layer's live figure count equals the pure helper and that the layer container is attached to the current street container with non-empty, on-screen bounds.
3. **Live population reconciliation still holds.** A reputation gain during a turn fades a figure in and a loss fades a figure out, delta-only, so the on-street count always tracks the HUD reputation value. Verified by the existing live-refresh test plus a scene-level assertion that the count is non-zero and matches `pedestrianCount(reputation)` after the first HUD refresh.
4. **Figures walk the roads and enter occupied businesses.** The documented road-lane walking, nearest-occupied-cell targeting, deliberate (non-teleporting) shop entry and crowd persistence across a street rebuild are retained. Verified by the existing pure/behaviour tests staying green and by a regression assertion that, by the reputation income phase, at least `PEDESTRIAN_MIN_SHOP_RATIO` (25%) of the live crowd is inside occupied cells.
5. **Reputation income is sourced from the crowd.** The `reputation` income phase keeps sourcing each business's coin flight from a figure inside that business (then a figure entering it, then any shopper, then a street anchor — never the HUD reputation counter), with the credited total unchanged. Verified by the existing income-phase source/invariant tests.
6. **Exemptions and determinism preserved.** Reduced Motion and replay/headless modes render no figures, no dissolve and no flights; the layer consumes no gameplay RNG (only the presentation-local PRNG) and a throwing layer never stalls the turn. Verified by existing exemption/determinism tests.
7. **Regression guard added.** A test that fails while the crowd is absent (e.g. a scene-level assertion of a non-empty, attached, visible layer at game start in normal play) is added so a future change cannot silently remove the crowd again. Verified by the new test failing on the pre-fix commit and passing on the fix.
8. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.**
9. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- **Restore, do not redesign.** The intended behaviour is the one documented in `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Ambient street pedestrians" and delivered by `MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E`; the fix restores it rather than introducing a new crowd design, ratio or choreography.
- **Presentation-only.** The layer and its dissolve must never mutate game state, the transcript or the turn flow; every entry point stays defensive so a bad frame cannot stall a turn.
- **No economy change.** Credited reputation income, the phase-sum invariant and the deferred-mutation handling are untouched.
- **Reduced Motion + replay/headless exemption** remain mandatory.
- **No new gameplay RNG consumption.** Any randomness stays in the presentation-local PRNG.
- **Minimal churn.** Touch only the pedestrian layer and the integration point(s) that caused the regression; do not undo unrelated panel/layout work.
- **Respect repository boundaries.** If the root cause is in the `core` submodule or shared UI, raise a separate core work item and record the dependency rather than editing the submodule silently.

## Existing state

- The feature exists and is wired in `dev`:
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — the layer (`pedestrianCount`, `buildRoadNetwork`, road-lane walking, shop entry, `startNewTurn`, `beginEndOfTurn`, `dissolveIntoCoins`, `setPopulation`, `update`).
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — constructs the layer, destroys it on shutdown and re-clamps it on resize.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — re-attaches the layer at the end of `refreshStreetGrid` after `streetContainer.removeAll(true)`.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — drives `msPedestrians.update(delta)` from the scene `update` loop.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `animateHudValueChanges` reconciles the population to `pedestrianCount(reputation)`; `dissolveReputationCoins` sources the reputation phase from the layer.
  - `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `startNewTurn()` on a new day and `beginEndOfTurn()` at end of turn.
- The feature shipped in **v0.1.19** (epic `MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E`, children listed under Related work).
- Documentation: `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` § "Ambient street pedestrians (reputation crowd)" describes the population rule, road walking, shop entry, live refresh, turn lifecycle, income conversion, accessibility and performance.
- The source file is unchanged since v0.1.19, so the regression is expected at an integration point changed after that release.

### Candidate causes to check (investigation starting points, not conclusions)

- **Attach/rebuild ordering:** `refreshStreetGrid` calls `streetContainer.removeAll(true)` (which destroys the layer's container) and re-attaches at the end; a new early return or reordering after v0.1.19 would leave the crowd destroyed.
- **Scene lifecycle:** the layer is re-created in two places in `createScene`; a second construction or a new boot path (new-game overlay, tutorial offer, checkpoint resume) may leave the live instance with `targetCount = 0`.
- **HUD refresh path:** the population is only reconciled from `animateHudValueChanges`; a change that bypasses, early-returns or defers that path (e.g. the display-only counting work) would stop `setPopulation` from running.
- **Render gating:** `isEnabled()` returns false when `replayMode` or `settingsPanel.reducedMotion` is true; a settings default change or a mis-detected replay mode would hide the layer.
- **Camera/mask/layout:** pedestrians are map-local children of the masked, camera-transformed street container; a layout, zoom or mask change can move or clip them off-screen while the slots stay visible.
- **Layer stacking:** the "UI simplification when roads are visible" epic made the market, hand and HUD panels opaque and moved the hand band; the crowd may be present but hidden behind a panel rather than absent.
- **End-of-turn timing:** the Turn Summary gate now defers the next day until **[ Next Turn ]**; during that dialog the crowd has already walked off the block, so "empty street" between turns is expected and must be distinguished from an empty street during a turn.

## Desired change

- Diagnose and fix the regression so the ambient reputation crowd is visible during normal play and the documented behaviour (road walking, shop entry, live reconciliation, crowd-sourced reputation income) is restored.
- Add the scene-level regression guard from AC7 so the layer cannot silently disappear again.
- Record the root cause and the guard in the work item and, where the documentation was thin on the lifecycle/attach contract, tighten `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` (or add a short note in `src/scenes/README.md`) so the next renderer change has a visible contract.
- Leave the economy, panel treatment, turn pacing and accessibility behaviour untouched.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts` — the layer; likely unchanged except a defensive fix if the root cause is in the layer.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — `refreshStreetGrid` attach ordering / early returns; prime suspect for a rebuild-time disappearance.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetScene.ts` — scene `update` loop and `getStreetContainer`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle.ts` — construction/re-construction, shutdown, resize.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorIncome.ts` — `syncPedestrianPopulation` / `animateHudValueChanges` / `dissolveReputationCoins`.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetAnimatorContext.ts` — animator accessors used by the dissolve path.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow.ts` — `startNewTurn` / `beginEndOfTurn` hooks and the Turn Summary gate.
- `src/scenes/MainStreetConstants.ts` — pedestrian constants (ratio, colour, size, speed, fade, shop ratio).
- `src/MainStreetMapView.ts` — road bands, viewport rect and camera transform used to place the layer.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-layer.test.ts` — pure/behaviour coverage of the layer.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-live-refresh.test.ts` — live reconciliation coverage.
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-count.test.ts` — population rule.
- `tests/main-street/income-phase-reputation-source.test.ts` / `income-phase-reputation-invariant.test.ts` — reputation-phase sourcing and credited-total invariants.
- `tests/main-street/` — new scene-level regression guard (e.g. `pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts`).
- `docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md` — pedestrian layer contract and lifecycle.
- `src/scenes/README.md` — scene module map / layer ownership note.

## Related work

- **MS-0MTV9AS15004AC1E** (completed) — "Visual representation of reputation": the epic that introduced the crowd; shipped in v0.1.19. This item is a regression against it.
- **MS-0MUYGFVVG009KONJ** (completed) — "Pedestrian count pure helper".
- **MS-0MUYGFW7T00579Z1** (completed) — "Pedestrian silhouette layer".
- **MS-0MUYGFWKG008GUA5** (completed) — "Live population reconciliation".
- **MS-0MUYGFWXK003QFYB** (completed) — "Reputation phase dissolve-to-coins".
- **MS-0MUYGFXA70009OWV** (completed) — "Pedestrian layer documentation".
- **MS-0MUYGFXMK009L1UU** (completed) — "Full-suite and build verification".
- **MS-0MUYGFVIJ00070MB** (completed) — "Reputation-phase invariant regression tests".
- **MS-0MUZ4WB290024ZGQ** (completed) — "Rework pedestrians: road-walking and shop-entry reputation source".
- **MS-0MUZ6CGSV002WTYM** (completed) — "Pedestrian polish: road lanes, deliberate shop entry, crowd persistence, end-of-turn walk-off".
- **MS-0MUZ9CKT60094CXO** (completed) — "In-shop pedestrians spread randomly across the occupied cell".
- **MS-0MUZ9O1I00088JF2** (completed) — "Pedestrians seek the nearest occupied cell (including mid-turn fills)".
- **MS-0MUZH6P0M00443G0** (completed) — "Spread reputation pedestrians evenly around the street edges".
- **MS-0MVKTB6WS000VLWK** (completed) — "UI simplification when roads are visible": opaque market/hand/HUD panels, hand-band move and Hint removal; a likely post-v0.1.19 integration change to check for occlusion or attach ordering.
- **MS-0MVP46Q8X003419R** / **MS-0MVP46AMO002SZUT** / **MS-0MVL6HMDP004WI41** (completed) — the Turn Summary dialog and its gate; changes the end-of-turn → next-day timing that drives `beginEndOfTurn` / `startNewTurn`.
- **MS-0MUYAESVU007X2U8** (completed) — "Coin and Reputation should count up/down": touched `animateHudValueChanges` and the HUD refresh path that reconciles the crowd.
- **MS-0MUR9IMN60093HIE** (completed) — "Re-tune reputation sources for the slower-coin economy": check that reputation units/ratios still yield a non-zero `pedestrianCount` at starting and mid-game reputation.
- **MS-0MV1BMMO900824N9** (completed) — "Restore Activity Log rendering": precedent for a renderer-rebuild regression (a container rebuild silently dropping a layer) and the style of guard/fix expected here.
- **MS-0MV1HJ9ES009Y8GK** (open) — "Migrate Main Street renderer from Canvas to WebGL": not a fix path, but relevant if the root cause is rendering-backend related.
- **docs/game/ux-visual-audio.md** — § "Ambient street pedestrians (reputation crowd)"; the authoritative behaviour contract this regression is measured against.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** "restore" means the documented v0.1.19 behaviour (1 figure per 50 reputation, road-lane walking, nearest-occupied-cell shop entry, live reconciliation, crowd-sourced reputation income), not a redesign.
- **Assumption:** the producer is playing normal single-player with default settings; Reduced Motion intentionally hides the crowd, and an empty street between turns (walk-off before **[ Next Turn ]**) is expected.
- **Risk: misdiagnosis as occlusion.** If the crowd is rendered but hidden behind the new opaque market/hand/HUD panels, "fixing" the layer would miss the cause. The reproduction must distinguish "not rendered" from "rendered but occluded/off-screen".
- **Risk: regression in a shared/core component.** The `core` pin has moved since v0.1.19; if the cause is in core's scene/UI plumbing, the fix must be a separate core work item with this item blocked on it.
- **Risk: no reliable scene-level test harness.** Existing pedestrian tests mock the scene and would not catch an integration regression. The guard must boot the real scene in a browser test (the repo already has `.browser.test.ts` coverage for the scene), or add the minimum harness needed.
- **Risk: end-of-turn timing confusion.** The Turn Summary gate can make the street look empty at a glance; the fix and tests must assert the crowd during a turn, not at the summary dialog.
- **Risk: determinism/perf regression.** Keep the presentation-only PRNG and the single shared texture; do not add per-figure gameplay RNG or unbounded cost.
- **Risk: scope creep.** Do not redesign the crowd, change the ratio/colour, or add new reputation visuals elsewhere; record such ideas as linked work items.
- **Assumption:** documentation may need only a small lifecycle/attach note if the root cause is an integration ordering bug; a full rewrite of the pedestrian section is out of scope.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **No producer questions were needed for intake.** The seed context plus the completed epic/documentation define the intended behaviour and the regression report is unambiguous; per the intake skill, the interview was skipped to avoid redundant questions. - Q (self, recorded as assumption): "Is the absence total or partial?" — **Assumption:** total absence in normal play; the brief allows for occlusion/off-screen as an alternative cause and requires the reproduction to distinguish them.
- Q (self, recorded as assumption): "Which mode?" — **Assumption:** normal single-player, default settings (Reduced Motion off, not replay/headless). The exemptions are explicitly out of scope.
- **Research summary:** the layer source and scene hooks are intact in `dev` (`src/scenes/MainStreetPedestrians.ts`, `MainStreetRendererStreet.refreshStreetGrid`, `MainStreetLifecycleManagerLifecycle`, `MainStreetScene.update`, `MainStreetAnimatorIncome.animateHudValueChanges`, `MainStreetTurnControllerTurnFlow`). The file is unchanged since v0.1.19, so the regression is at an integration point; the candidate list above narrows the search to attach ordering, lifecycle re-creation, HUD refresh gating, render gating, camera/mask/layout and layer stacking. Existing pedestrian tests use a mock scene and would not catch this class of failure, which motivates the scene-level guard in AC7.

## Related work (automated report)

**Decision:** full planning required (effort/risk pre-check returned `decision: plan`; effort Small, risk High). Approval gate returned `request_approval: false` — approval is only requested for Extra Large effort **and** High/Severe risk, so planning proceeded through the automated review stages without a producer pause.

| # | Feature | Type | Priority | Depends on | Parent ACs |
|---|---------|------|----------|-----------|------------|
| 1 | Reproduce and diagnose the crowd regression (`MS-0MVRMHS4S0067RRQ`) | task | high | — | 1 |

### Vertical slice check

Each item delivers an end-to-end increment for its concern rather than a single horizontal layer: the diagnosis item produces reproducible evidence + a recorded root cause; each test item produces a runnable scene-level suite plus the red/green evidence trail; the fix item produces the user-visible behaviour together with its own verification and comment trail; docs deliver the contract next to the code; verification delivers build + suite + smoke evidence. # Phaser 4 + WebGL: `GeometryMask` `setMask` is a no-op, so the street map and log viewports are unclipped

Discovered-from: MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q (reputation crowd regression diagnosis, MS-0MVRMHS4S0067RRQ).

## Problem

The game runs Phaser `4.0.0-rc.7`. In Phaser 4 the WebGL renderer no longer supports `GameObject.setMask` with a `GeometryMask`; it logs and returns immediately:

```js
// node_modules/phaser/src/gameobjects/components/Mask.js
setMask: function (mask) {
    if (this.scene.renderer.type === CONST.WEBGL) {
        console.warn('Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.');
        return this;
    }
```

Observed on every street refresh of the real scene (WebGL, normal play):

```
Phaser.GameObjects.Components.Mask.setMask: This method is not supported in WebGL. Create a Mask filter instead.
```

Call sites in this repo that therefore do nothing under WebGL:

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:611` — `s.streetContainer.setMask(mask)` (the street map viewport mask, `installStreetMapMask` / `updateStreetMapMask`)
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts:331` — `s.logContentContainer.setMask(s.logContentMask)` (Activity Log scroll clipping)
- core: `core/src/ui/HelpPanel.ts:524`, `core/src/ui/Overlay.ts:484`, `core/src/ui/SettingsPanel.ts:909` (core-owned; raise/route in core rather than editing the submodule)

Consequences in the real (WebGL) game: the street map is no longer clipped to the street viewport (it can draw over neighbouring panels/outside its band) and the Activity Log content is no longer clipped to its scroll area. The Canvas path (used by most browser tests) still honours the masks, so the regression is invisible to the test suite.

## Notes / scope

- Not the cause of the crowd regression: an unclipped container renders *more*, not less, and the crowd was verified present, attached, textured and on-screen under WebGL (see `tests/main-street/pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts`).
- Fix direction: Phaser 4 mask **filters** (`createMaskFilter` / `Filters.Mask`) for the WebGL path, or a renderer-agnostic clipping approach; verify visually in the real WebGL build and keep the Canvas behaviour unchanged.
- Discovered while diagnosing MS-0MVRDVVH4001048Q; no fix attempted there (out of scope).

## Acceptance criteria (provisional — refine at intake/plan)

1. The street map viewport is clipped to `streetViewportRect` in the real WebGL renderer (no rendering outside the band; map scroll/zoom still clipped as before).
2. The Activity Log content is clipped to its scroll area under WebGL.
3. No `setMask … not supported in WebGL` console warning remains in a real-scene WebGL boot (assert in a browser test on the real renderer).
4. Canvas rendering behaviour and the existing layout/panel tests stay green; the full suite passes.
5. Core-owned call sites are fixed upstream (core work item) or explicitly documented as deferred.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `src/scenes/MainStreetRendererStreet.ts` — street map mask + log mask call sites
- `src/scenes/MainStreetRenderer.ts` / `MainStreetRendererContext.ts` — mask install/update wiring
- `tests/main-street/pedestrians-scene-visibility.browser.test.ts` (existing WebGL boot harness to reuse for a console-warning assertion)
- `docs/dev/` — note the Phaser 4 WebGL mask restriction next to the renderer docs
